title: DR1 shows the draft status and the notification reference from the first page of a new notification; the frontend withholds both until the first answer is saved.

finding.frontend: A strip carrying a blue "Draft" tag and the notification reference sits above the page heading on 29 of the 33 captured screens. Origin of the import is the one journey page without it: on a brand-new notification the page shows the heading with nothing above it, so the user starting a notification cannot see its reference until they have saved the first page. The strip is suppressed deliberately — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:88-89 passes the journey to the layout only once the notification has committed answers, and src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:65-70 renders nothing when it is absent.
finding.prototype: DR1's origin page shows the strip unconditionally: a "Draft" tag and the reference GBN-AG-26-7K8M2P sit between the back link and the caption, exactly as they do on every later page. The view includes the shared status partial with no guard at all — app/views/origin-of-the-import.html:29 — and app/views/partials/notification-status.html:18-24 defaults the status text to "Draft" when nothing has set one, which is what makes the strip work on a notification that has not been touched yet.
finding.difference: Render the status strip on Origin of the import from the first request, by dropping the committed-answers guard at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:88-89 so the journey always reaches the layout. Nothing blocks it: the reference already exists when the page is first drawn. Starting a notification posts to the backend, which mints the reference and returns the created record, and the user is only then redirected to the origin page under that reference — so the reference is in the page's own URL before a single answer is saved. The guard is a presentation choice, not a symptom of a missing reference. The back-link target on the same page is computed from the same condition and is correct as it stands — a fresh notification's back link goes to the dashboard — so change only the strip, keeping `backLinkFor` on the committed-answers test.
finding.falsifiedBy: Loading Origin of the import on a notification with no saved answers and seeing a Draft tag and reference above the heading.
finding.correction: Claim sound, and the assumption it rested on is now settled in its favour, so the hedge has been replaced with the answer. The reference does exist before the first save. `startJourney` calls `records.create()` (src/server/app/engine/journey.js:46-51), the real adapter POSTs to the backend, which mints the reference and returns the created notification (src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/create.js:7-17), and the dashboard's create handler then redirects to the origin page under that id (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/controller.js:115-118). The captured frontend origin screen's own URL is `/notifications/GBN-XX-00-REFERENCE/origin`, which is the reference. So the finding is about a styling guard and not about record ordering. Counts re-derived: 29 of 33 frontend DOMs carry `app-journey-strip` and the four without are the confirmation, the two dashboards and origin, so "the one journey page without it" is exact; 32 of 40 DR1 DOMs carry `app-notification-status`. Two notes that do not change the finding. The default-to-Draft behaviour is at app/views/partials/notification-status.html:3, not at the cited :18-24 — :18-24 is the DR1 branch that renders the strip, which is what the cited range actually shows. And the DR1 screens without the strip are not only the dashboards and the confirmation: DR1 also omits it from its declaration and from all three transporter-add pages, where the frontend shows it. That is a difference in the opposite direction, it is not this finding, and no finding in this slice claims it; it reads as prototype drift rather than a rule, since DR1 states no reason a sub-form should lose the strip.
